answers.core: There is a reason, everything is the same as with the `is_inf` and `is_nan` methods. After all, they can be replaced with entries `value != INF and value != -INF` and `value != NAN`
answers.workaround: If this is not used often, then it can be implemented in a few lines of script. But checking this exception may be required anywhere in any project.
